org.name: Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust

theme: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

reports.title: Patricia Cleghorn
categories: Community health care and emergency services related deaths

promises.quote: Creation of an urgent care assessment team to concentrate specifically on the assessment of patients who are in crisis. This approach has been piloted and has demonstrated that having an urgent care assessment team improves outcomes for patients at this vulnerable time. The substantive team will be in place by the end of September 2016
promises.summary: Urgent care assessment team to improve crisis patient assessment

promises.quote: One consultant psychiatrist will form part of each home treatment team to ensure that all patients who are presenting high levels of risk have daily access to medical review or medical opinion. This will be in place across all of our home treatment teams by the end of October 2016
promises.summary: Consultant psychiatrist in each home treatment team for daily risk review

promises.quote: We will take action with regards to managing the breach of policy The Senior Nurse for Professional Standards issued a formal practice alert on 12th September 2016 to registered and unregistered clinicians in our crisis and community teams to reinforce the requirements for: Clinical Risk Assessments regarding risk of self-harm and/or suicide; Risk Assessments with regard to medicines management and self-medication; Safe administration of medication as per current Medicines Code and NMC Code.
promises.summary: Formal practice alert on risk and medication assessments issued

promises.quote: NHS England recently established an adult mental health programme which is taking a whole system approach comprising crisis, acute, and community/primary care work streams. The acute care work stream has been developed in response to a number of recommendations set out by the Commission on Acute Adult Psychiatric Care and The Five Year Forward View for Mental Health, and is particularly relevant to the concerns outlined in your report.
promises.summary: Establish adult mental health programme with acute care work stream to address lack of acute beds and risk assessment concerns

concerns.quote: availability of acute mental health beds means the most vulnerable people are being cared for in the community with limited resources and care
concerns.hazard: lack of acute mental health beds

concerns.quote: The deceased had repeatedly stated that she would end her life by taking an overdose
No formal risk assessment was undertaken and staff failed to appreciate what drugs she had available to her

reports.title: Leroy Hamilton: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: Lack of inpatient mental health beds and lack of Psychiatric decisions unit (PDU) spaces
concerns.hazard: lack of inpatient mental health beds and PDU spaces

concerns.quote: it is often the case that due to the lack of inpatient beds and PDU spaces patients are often left in the Emergency department unattended or sent home with periodic reviews by the home treatment team whilst waiting for a bed
concerns.hazard: lack of inpatient beds and PDU spaces

concerns.quote: there is no agreed protocol to deal with informal patients who abscond from emergency departments
concerns.hazard: lack of agreed protocol for informal missing patients

concerns.quote: on 2 occasions (03/12/21 and 07/12/21) there was a failure to treat Mr Hamilton as a missing person when he was reported as missing
concerns.hazard: failure to treat missing persons as high risk

concerns.quote: When Mr Hamilton was first reported as missing no risk assessment was undertaken about his level of risk to himself
concerns.hazard: lack of risk assessment for missing persons

links.explanation: Both reports highlight a lack of proper risk assessment concerning individuals at risk of self‑harm. The earlier case involved medication availability while the later case involves missing‑person risk assessment.
